title: Deep learning identifies morphological patterns of homologous recombination deficiency in luminal breast cancers from whole slide images

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Deep learning identifies morphological patterns of homologous recombination deficiency in luminal breast cancers from whole slide images》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Homologous recombination DNA-repair deficiency (HRD) is becoming a well-recognized marker of platinum salt and polyADP-ribose polymerase inhibitor chemotherapies in ovarian and breast cancers.

evidence.text: Homologous recombination DNA-repair deficiency (HRD) is becoming a well-recognized marker of platinum salt and polyADP-ribose polymerase inhibitor chemotherapies in ovarian and breast cancers.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Deep learning identifies morphological patterns of homologous recombination deficiency in luminal breast cancers from whole slide images》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】With the objectives of providing a robust deep-learning method for HRD prediction from tissue slides and identifying related morphological phenotypes, we first show that digital pathology workflows are sensitive to potential biases in the training set, then we propose a method to overcome the influence of these biases, and we develop an interpretation method capable of identifying complex phenotypes.

evidence.text: With the objectives of providing a robust deep-learning method for HRD prediction from tissue slides and identifying related morphological phenotypes, we first show that digital pathology workflows are sensitive to potential biases in the training set, then we propose a method to overcome the influence of these biases, and we develop an interpretation method capable of identifying complex phenotypes.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Deep learning identifies morphological patterns of homologous recombination deficiency in luminal breast cancers from whole slide images》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】Application to our carefully curated in-house dataset allows us to predict HRD with high accuracy (area under the receiver-operator characteristics curve 0.86) and to identify morphological phenotypes related to HRD.
